```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# brand colours, site data (respondents, panel, variables) and figure theme
source(here::here("R", "site.R"))
```

```{r}
#| label: thumbnail
#| include: false
# Card image for the listings: a simple version of the main figure, without
# any text, on the tint background. Saved next to this page.
thumbnail <- respondents |>
  summarise(mean = mean(lr), .by = dataset) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = mean, y = dataset, colour = dataset)) +
  geom_point(size = 6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = dataset_colours, guide = "none") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = brand[["tint"]], colour = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(18, 18, 18, 18)
  )

ggsave("thumbnail.png", thumbnail, width = 6, height = 3.9, dpi = 150)
```

<!-- Chunk labels must not start with "fig-": that makes Quarto number the

One or two paragraphs that say what this page looks at and why it matters.

::: {.how-to-read}
How to read the figure below, in one or two sentences.
:::

```{r}
#| label: plot-first
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-alt: "Describe what the figure shows, including the main pattern."
respondents |>
  summarise(mean = mean(lr), .by = dataset) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = mean, y = dataset, colour = dataset)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = dataset_colours, guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "A one-line takeaway",
    x = "Mean on the scale",
    y = NULL,
    caption = site_caption
  )
```

What the figure shows, with numbers as inline R.
